Bragg Curve and Bragg peak
 The Bragg curve describes the energy loss of charged
particles as they travel through matter.
 At the beginning of their path, the particles lose only a
small amount of energy per unit distance.
 As the particles slow down, the rate of energy loss
gradually increases.
 Near the end of their range, the particles deposit a
maximum amount of energy in a very localized region —
this is called the Bragg peak.
 After this point, the particles stop and no longer cause
ionization.

DNA Lesions
DNA Damage from Ionizing Radiation:
 Double-strand breaks: Irreparable when opposite → cell
death.
 Single-strand breaks: Usually repairable, unless lesions
accumulate causing replication failure.
 Base damage: Destruction/modification → mutations.
 Sugar damage: Deoxyribose degradation → backbone
instability.
 Cross-links: DNA–DNA / DNA–protein → structural
distortion: interferes with replication and transcription.
